Yes, you can absolutely run Docker with the standard Docker Engine and Docker with Sysbox on the same host machine simultaneously. [1, 2, 3, 4] 
In fact, this is exactly how Sysbox is intended to be used. Sysbox is not a replacement for the Docker Engine; it is an alternative container runtime (called sysbox-runc) that integrates directly into your existing Docker Engine infrastructure. [1, 2, 5, 6] 
## How They Coexist
When you install the [Nestybox Sysbox runtime](https://github.com/nestybox/sysbox) on your machine, it registers itself alongside Docker's standard runtime (runc). Your host runs a single Docker daemon (dockerd), but you gain the ability to choose which runtime executes your containers on a case-by-case basis. [1, 2, 3, 6, 7] 
## Launching Standard vs. Sysbox Containers
You can split workloads dynamically by specifying the runtime flag in your CLI commands: [2, 8] 


* 
* Standard Docker Container: By default, Docker uses runc.


docker run -d --name standard-nginx nginx


* Sysbox "System" Container: To use Sysbox's advanced isolation (perfect for Docker-in-Docker or running Systemd), simply add the --runtime flag.


docker run --runtime=sysbox-runc -d --name secure-dind-node nestybox/ubuntu-noble-systemd-docker


[1, 8, 9, 10, 11] 
* 


## Configuring Runtimes via Daemon Configuration
You can inspect or manage how Docker handles both runtimes by looking at your /etc/docker/daemon.json configuration file. During installation, Sysbox automatically updates this file to register itself: [3, 12, 13] 


{
  "runtimes": {
    "sysbox-runc": {
      "path": "/usr/bin/sysbox-runc"
    }
  }
}


If you ever want all of your containers to automatically use Sysbox without explicitly typing the flag every time, you can set it as the global default by adding "default-runtime": "sysbox-runc" to that same file. However, keeping the standard runc as the default and targeting Sysbox explicitly is the most common approach for hybrid environments. [2, 14, 15] 
If you run into any issues during setup, let me know if you would like help with:
Installing Sysbox on your specific Linux distributionConfiguring Docker-in-Docker (DinD) using SysboxSetting up Docker Compose to handle both runtimes
